These are the agencies' own research-subject classifications used on the application forms, not university majors; the scholarship is held in whatever doctoral programme the student is registered in.

SSHRC table: 32 lines were left out: the catch-all "Other ..." lines, and two Literature lines whose names are cut off in the PDF text (codes 52000 and 52099). Interdisciplinary Studies (70000) and Women's Studies (70100) are main disciplines in the table.

SSHRC states that "Health" can only be an Entry 2 or Entry 3 discipline, never the main one; priority research areas (digital technologies, health and biotechnology, clean technology, environment/climate/Arctic, food and water security, democratic resilience, advanced manufacturing and materials, defence and dual-use) give no field restriction and are not merit-reviewed.
NSERC code table also lists area-of-application and industry codes; those are not fields of study and were not recorded.
